question: There are mainly ______ main processes of change of population.
solution:
The correct answer is __**3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Change in population** occurs primarily due to three main processes: **birth rate, death rate, and migration**. These are the fundamental factors influencing population dynamics.
 
• The **birth rate** refers to the number of live births per thousand people in a year. It contributes to the increase in population.
 
• The **death rate** is the number of deaths per thousand people in a year. A lower death rate leads to population growth, while a higher one can decrease it.
 
• **Migration** involves the movement of people from one place to another. It can be internal (within a country) or international (between countries). Migration affects the distribution and size of the population in different regions.
 
• These three processes—birth rate, death rate, and migration—are essential for understanding population trends and patterns globally. *Hence, the correct answer is 3.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Birth Rate:**

 
 
• The birth rate is expressed as the number of live births per 1,000 individuals per year.
 
• Countries with a high birth rate often experience rapid population growth, especially in developing nations.
 
• For example, in 2021, countries like **Niger** had one of the highest birth rates globally.
 
 
 
• **Death Rate:**
 
 
• It is the number of deaths per 1,000 individuals per year.
 
• Advancements in healthcare and sanitation have significantly lowered death rates worldwide, particularly in developed nations.
 
• For instance, countries like **Japan** have a low death rate due to their excellent healthcare system.
 
 
 
• **Migration:**
 
 
• Migration is categorized into immigration (moving into a new area) and emigration (moving out of an area).
 
• Migration can be driven by factors like economic opportunities, conflict, natural disasters, and education.
 
• For example, the **Syrian refugee crisis** saw millions of people migrating to other countries.
 
 
 
• **Population Growth:**
 
 
• Population growth is determined by the balance between birth rate and death rate, coupled with the net migration rate.
 
• Countries like **India** and **China** have seen significant population growth, while countries like **Japan** face population decline due to a low birth rate and high aging population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Demographic Transition Theory:**

 
 
• This theory explains population change over time based on the birth and death rates.
 
• It has four stages: high stationary, early expanding, late expanding, and low stationary.
 
• Developed countries are in the last stage, while many developing nations are in the second or third stage.
 
 
 
• **Global Population Trends:**
 
 
• The world population reached **8 billion** in **2022**, as per the **United Nations**.
 
• Regions like **Sub-Saharan Africa** are expected to see the highest population growth by 2050.
